findings.text: follow-on: the reviewed run's manifest records baseline_suite and after_suite as null although its declared write paths include a test file, so the two gate arms exist only as free text in test_logs and before-*.log; a reader that looks for the arms in the structured keys finds nothing and must reconstruct the delta from the before-summary.txt line PASSES=5 FAILS=5 and the gate logs. The arms were measured and are readable, so this is a record-shape gap, not missing evidence: the offline derivation here reads added_failure_count 0 and added_failure_ids [] from before-{1..10}.log (5 failed of 10 of test_a_dispatch_confirms_its_supervisor_reached_the_run, FileNotFoundError on worker.json) against gate-repeat.log (PASSES=20 FAILS=0) and gate-file.log (5 passed EXIT=0).

justifications.durability: the fix routes the worker.json read through the file's own bounded _wait_for (tests/test_fleet_lane_carries_the_dispatch_environment.py:82, WAIT_SECONDS 20.0, fail with a named message rather than hanging), so a record that never arrives fails cleanly; the stub worker sleeps 60 s (fixture line ~225) so the following exit.json absence assertion is not itself exposed to the same race, and the id passed 20 of 20 alone.
justifications.evidence: a differential arm exists on both sides: before-{1..10}.log show 5 failed / 5 passed of the single id at base c952174a7 with FileNotFoundError on worker.json, gate-repeat.log shows 20 of 20 passes at head b75238a53, and the declared negative control (delayed-write-* / negative-control.log) reddens the parent commit's test deterministically (1 failed, worker.json FileNotFoundError, EXIT=1) while the head arm stays green (EXIT=0). An independent whole-file re-run in the reviewed worktree at 94c799c3e reproduced 5 passed / EXIT=0.
justifications.fit: the change reuses the existing _wait_for helper the marker wait already calls, adds no import, and its comment states the write-ordering mechanism (marker at worker start vs worker.json after the spawn returns) rather than the ticket; both commits are conventional with bodies, no plan or ticket identifiers appear in source or messages, and the evidence fragment follows the repository's docs/evidence/fragments shape. The record-shape finding on the manifest is the one deduction.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the node's stated goal is that the supervised-dispatch test wait for the worker record before reading it, and the diff does exactly that (tests/test_fleet_lane_carries_the_dispatch_environment.py:344-349): it adds a bounded wait on worker.json before the read at the line that raced. The named cause is confirmed in the product the test exercises -- the supervisor writes WORKER_RECORD_NAME via _write_attempt_artifact at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:10326-10339, after the _supervisor_spawn_worker call at :10306 -- so the marker (written as the stub worker starts) does not imply the record exists. No failing test is disabled, skipped or deleted and no assertion was weakened.
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff c952174a7..94c799c3e touches exactly the two declared write paths (the test file and one docs/evidence fragment) with 43 insertions and 2 deletions; no file under reckon/ or any skill or SPA source changed, and the worktree is clean at head.
